articles.title: Cool as a cucumber: recipes and tips to save you from cooking in a heatwave | Kitchen aide
articles.summary: When ovens and stovetops just won’t do, turn to loaded toasts, open sandwiches, cold noodles and smashed cucumbers, say our no-cook experts. It’s too hot to turn on the oven or stove. What can I make for dinner that’s still substantial?
body: Otherwise, Mark could do away with the toaster and get some focaccia, suggests Jamie Pickles, chef/co-owner of Stow and The Trof, both in Manchester: “Mix picked brown crab meat with mayo, lemon juice and mustard, and spread that over the bread.” Next, combine the picked white meat with chopped chives and coriander, lemon juice, creme fraiche and black pepper. “Mix through some tinned sweetcorn, spread that over the brown crab mayo and finish with watercress.”
articles.author: Anna Berrill

articles.title: The hill I will die on: Packing light is for cowards. Pack heavy | Max Olesker
articles.summary: Trip-prepping shouldn’t be a grim exercise in minimising your milligrams. Take day outfits, night outfits, gymwear, swimwear – and prepare for an adventure. If you’re on the hunt for a streamlined way to travel internationally while only packing a toothbrush, an iPad, a single white T-shirt made of…
body: Packing for travel shouldn’t be a grim logistical exercise in minimising the milligrams of mass one must transport. It should be a prelude to an adventure – and an adventure in itself!

(Suit)case in point, I have recently embarked on a journey to the Edinburgh fringe, where – after many years as a double-act comedian – I am performing my first ever solo theatre show. Thus, I have packed what I deem the essentials – which is to say, for every possible eventuality.

Dressing up. Dressing down. A dressing gown (and pyjamas and slippers, naturally). Gymwear, swimwear. Day outfits, night outfits, show outfits. A series of mysterious items for vocal rest (Dr Nelson’s legendary inhaler). Books! More books! Face masks (why not?).
I’ve no interest in dull consumerism – but there is a joy in choice; a power in seeing what the universe has to hurl at you that day, and reaching into your luggage to meet the moment.
articles.author: Max Olesker

articles.title: Match review – gory and slyly satirical catfishing horror for the age of Hinge
articles.summary: Online dating’s eternal bugbear reaches a horrific apotheosis in this funny, grimy and impishly directed shocker. Paola (Humberly González) is a pretty young woman about to turn 30 who hasn’t found herself a steady boyfriend – so, like many people of her generation, she’s on all the dating apps.
body: Of course, Paola should have listened to her sister. The good looking guy (played by Luke Volker) turns out to have been a catfishing lure, and the real Henry (Jacques Adriaanse) looks like what you’d get if a troll mated with a slime mould. Plus, it’s actually Henry’s deranged mother, Lucille (a fantastic Dianne Simpson) who’s been writing all those courtly messages to Paola – who is soon sedated with drugged wine and wakes up about to be raped, exactly the sort of scenario your actual mother warned you about.

Fortunately, it’s not all grim worst-nightmare-ever stuff, thanks to a slyly witty script credited to Al Kaplan and Jon Kaplan, directed with impish verve by Danishka Esterhazy. There are some very funny scenes, including a great two-hander between Lucille and another possible victim, Natalie (Nikita Faber), who hasn’t been completely honest about her own presentation online. The last stretch has lashings of practical effect gore to keep the genre fans happy, but it’s the sour social satire that lingers in the imagination afterwards.
articles.author: Leslie Felperin

articles.title: Laughing on the other side: the fringe shows turning painful breakups into comedy
articles.summary: Whether Elf Lyons’ high-concept Hollywood throwback, Kate Dehnert’s disorientating rave or Ele McKenzie’s Bob Dylan fantasy, heartbreak fuels fine humour at the festival. Breakups. We’ve all been through them. Sometimes they’re mutual, sometimes not. Sometimes agony, sometimes relief.
body: Perhaps formal innovation isn’t such a shock when Elf Lyons is the innovator, as almost all of this dedicated nonconformist’s work has been entirely bespoke. But even for her, The Woman on the Edge is something different: shards of a disintegrating sense of self, grafted together to suggest the journey Lyons has been on since her relationship ended, shortly before her wedding day, early last year. The conceit is that the show is being performed by a Norma Desmond-alike alter ego. A brittle and wise-cracking refugee from vintage Hollywood, smoke plumes from her décolletage as she fills in for absent Elf while keeping at bay her husband, the clown Pagliacci, on the end of the phone.

But that conceit soon devolves to others: audio clips of Lyons, her friends and family talking about her breakup and subsequent breakdown; scenes from an ill-advised romantic tryst in Thailand; an “opera” spliced together from remarks made to Lyons by self-absorbed men. There’s a subplot about the Apollo 13 mission, a private passion of Lyons’, which emerges as a metaphor for her search for fulfilment in love. All might look lost, but mission control could yet bring the crew home alive.
articles.author: Brian Logan

articles.title: Dickovers, baggravation and botiquette: 18 new words to describe our tech hellscape
articles.summary: There are many tech irritants that are a scourge of modern life, yet we have lacked the vocabulary to describe them... until now. The “dickover” is the scourge of the modern age.
body: We shouldn’t fool ourselves into thinking that dickovers are the only terrible thing about technology in 2026. Until now, though, we have lacked the vocabulary to describe them, so here are some suggestions.

The worst part of the internet is that it is now impossible to escape AI features because they are shoehorned into everything. Google gives you an AI overview before you get to your search results. Instagram can create AI images. Spotify has an AI DJ that can talk between songs for some reason. None of this is useful. My car just switched from Google Assistant (“Sure, navigating to KFC”) to Google Gemini (“OK, great. I’ve noticed a number of locations within 100 miles of you that contain the letters ‘K’, ‘F’ and ‘C’. Give me a little more information on where you’re heading and I’ll get straight to showing you the way”). Shut up you water-guzzling idiot and give me my chicken.

articles.title: Banana Republic Just Dropped the Transitional Pieces You’ll Wear Into Fall
articles.summary: Between its summer essentials, relaxed workwear, and wanderlust-inducing styles, the retailer’s latest drops feel primed for the season ahead.
body: With a few weeks to go before Labor Day, summer is still very much here, but fall dressing is already starting to feel increasingly tempting. Banana Republic’s latest new arrivals offer plenty of options for both sides of this transitional stretch.

Elsewhere, some of fall’s biggest trends make an appearance. Funnel-neck silhouettes offer a more dramatic update to staple jackets and tops, while utilitarian influences show up in cargo pants and other pocket-heavy, buckle-adorned pieces. Lace-trimmed detailing provides a softer counterpoint, bringing a romantic element to camisoles and separates that can be dressed up or down. There’s still plenty for anyone not ready to leave summer behind, too. Printed slip skirts, lightweight dresses, and barely-there tank tops are made for warm evenings and last-minute vacation plans.

In the handbags department, raffia styles are decidedly seasonal and fun. Meanwhile, roomier totes lend themselves to multiple uses: spacious enough to function as everyday carryalls, but large enough to double as getaway bags for one final weekend out of town.
articles.author: Irina Grechko

articles.title: 24 Best Bridal Pajamas for the Wedding, Honeymoon, and Beyond
articles.summary: You have the dress—now, shop Vogue’s edit of the best bridal pajamas, sets, and robes to ensure you start your wedding day on the right foot.
body: The big white dress gets a lot of attention—but in the run-up to your big day, you start to realize exactly how many bridal extras you may need. From the rehearsal dinner to the bridal shower to, yes, the loungewear you’ll wear to sip your coffee and get ready the morning-of, weddings come with a lot of outfit changes. Why not have fun with it? Bridal pajamas take on many forms—and the best ones, complete with feather embellishments and silky fabrics, are really pretty fabulous.

Think of it as your way to set the tone for the day. Choose a satin robe to match an opulent setting, a breezy cotton set to mirror a coastal destination, or a beautifully detailed slip dress that makes you feel put-together just by throwing it on. One thing to keep in mind: Whatever sleepwear you choose, opt for something you can slip on or off without compromising your hair and makeup.

Whatever you gravitate to, it’ll serve as a memento of your special morning long after the day is done; choose wisely. From perfectly bridal pajama sets to sweet robes to delicate nightgowns both long and short, here are 24 options to consider.
articles.author: Lea Donenberg

articles.title: Dylan Meyer and Shatara Michelle Ford on Remaking Genre Movies in Their Own Image
articles.summary: The filmmakers behind “The Wrong Girls” and “Dreams in Nightmares” have reimagined two classic tropes—the buddy comedy and the road movie—for a different time (and different bodies).
body: When I tell filmmaker Shatara Michelle Ford that I don’t want to pin down Dreams in Nightmares, their elegiac sophomore feature, explicitly as a “road movie”—that it feels too slippery, too much its own thing, to sit neatly inside a genre built on decades of lone men and empty highways—they stop me, considerately.

“I appreciate you not wanting to put it in a genre bucket,” they say. “But the whole thing that I do is a revisionist exercise with all things. So this is a revisionist road movie. It’s definitely that.”

“I like to think of the obvious, Hollywoodized, uncomplex version of the thing that I’m trying to do, and then I intentionally undo it,” Ford explains. “Not that I would have made the Hollywood version anyway. I’m having a conversation with that the whole time.”

A few weeks earlier, Dylan Meyer was describing a similar instinct in her own directorial debut, The Wrong Girls —a profane, druggy stoner comedy about two aimless best friends who accidentally steal a suitcase stocked with vials of an experimental drug. There are talking cats, Dutch criminals, and telepathy. The protagonists, notably, are women.

articles.title: The Exec’s Guide to Longevity Tech
articles.summary: AI is reshaping preventative health just as longevity becomes one of luxury’s fastest-growing opportunities. Where is the technology heading next, and what should fashion execs be paying attention to?
body: Living longer is the new luxury. Once confined to biotech labs and the disposable income of Silicon Valley billionaires, longevity is no longer a tech bro hobby and has become a consumer aspiration in its own right. Preventative full-body MRI scans, AI-powered health dashboards and wearable biometric trackers are rapidly moving from niche health tools to status symbols, particularly among affluent consumers and celebrity ambassadors.

The CEOs of many of the leading players in the space say their fastest-growing consumer categories are Gen Z and post-menopausal women. For the ultra-rich, healthspan — the proportion of one’s life spent living in good health — has become one of the few remaining assets that money can meaningfully improve.

articles.title: The Secret to Sliceable No-Bake Cheesecake
articles.summary: This one ingredient ensures your filling doesn’t slump.
body: Welcome to Bon Appétit Bake Club, a community of curious bakers. Each month senior test kitchen editors Jesse Szewczyk and Shilpa Uskokovic share a must-make recipe and dive deep on why it works. Come bake and learn with us— ask questions, share pics, listen to our podcast, and lots more here. And don't forget to join the Bake Club Group chat over on Substack.

Intimated by using gelatin? Let me break it down for you. By using a rather conservative amount (just one packet, or roughly 2½ tsp.) you avoid the infamous wiggle-jiggle. This small amount is enough to hold everything in place, while keeping the texture supple and creamy, not firm and bouncy.

To use it, you first need to bloom the gelatin in a little bit of cold water. This process dissolves the gelatin, ensuring there are no lumps in your final product. (Simply adding the gelatin to warm liquid is a recipe for disaster.) Because the filling is made in the mixer, you’ll bloom the gelatin directly in the mixer bowl for one less dish to clean.
articles.author: Jesse Szewczyk

articles.title: The Saint-Tropez Scene May Seem Impenetrable—Here Are Our 10 Unwritten Rules for Making the Most of It
articles.summary: There are laws, and then there is protocol.
body: Brigitte Bardot may be gone, but the mythology she unwittingly created in Roger Vadim's 1956 And God Created Woma n still defines how the world imagines Saint-Tropez: a world of sun-kissed shores, seduction, and carefree abandon. But that enchantment began long before the beach clubs and celebrity sightings. Back in 1892, French artist Paul Signac dropped anchor here, encouraging friends such as Henri Matisse and André Derain to follow. And in the 1920s, weary of Paris, the writer Colette settled near Plage des Salins, finding joy in picking figs and lemons from her garden, dancing at open-air balls with young sailors—and eventually declaring she'd found paradise.

Today's cast of characters is more likely to include billionaires, influencers, and a new generation chasing the White Lotus fantasy. Yet Saint-Tropez remains stubbornly itself, with social rituals and unspoken conventions that aren't always obvious at first. Knowing them won't just help you avoid the occasional faux pas; they'll help you navigate the village like a pro.
La Réserve à la Plage is a more demure beach club option, at least aesthetically.

articles.title: The 15 Most Beautiful Airport Landings in the World, Ranked
articles.summary: Flying to any of these destinations? You'll want to bag a window seat.
body: Whether you’re a seasoned jetsetter or a first-time flier, few things compare to the bird's-eye vista that comes into focus during the most beautiful airport landings in the world. While the long-legged aisle-hoggers among us might not relate, travelers lucky enough to settle into the window seat on certain flight routes can look forward to quite the show ahead of touchdown.
Plane travel is the only means of transport onto and off the island for all tourists and locals on Lord Howe Island, New South Wales, Australia.

To uncover the most beautiful airport landings in the world, AllClear Travel Insurance analyzed 32 airports around the world known for the dazzling views ahead of the runway. One hundred participants were presented with a series of images showcasing the airport runways, and their visual engagement was measured using eye-tracking technology to determine the most captivating landings. The speed at which participants first focused on an image, and the average length of time participants spent looking at each image, were both recorded and turned into a score.
